chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: "The owner of the goods has more right to bargain."
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to initiate bargaining in a sale according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the seller's priority in initiating price negotiations, reflecting the Prophetic tradition of fairness and transparency in commercial transactions. It underscores the ethical principle that the owner of the goods holds the primary right to set the initial terms, thereby preventing coercion and ensuring mutual consent in the marketplace.
